title: Latency-Aware Selective Verification in Generate–Validate NetOps Pipelines: A Confirmatory Paired Study with gpt-5-mini
abstract: We study whether a selective, low-latency verification tier (risk-scoring + fast validator) inserted into a generate–validate–repair pipeline reduces unsafe commits from LLM-generated network changes while meeting operational latency constraints. We preregistered a paired confirmatory design (CAND-2026-001): 400 synthetic operator intents (10% adversarial/OOD) were presented to gpt-5-mini under two conditions (baseline: LLM-only; guarded: selective verifier). The primary estimand was the paired reduction in unsafe-commit rate against a full-checker ground truth. Results on the preregistered confirmatory set: baseline 399/400 successful (valid) generations; guarded 400/400 successful generations; paired difference = 0.0025 (0.25 percentage points), two-sided exact McNemar p = 1.0, 95% paired bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.0075]. The guarded pipeline produced one discordant pair (guarded succeeded where baseline failed), but the absolute effect is small and not statistically distinguishable from zero in this test. We report methodology, preregistration, deterministic execution artifacts, and an explicit discussion of limits: synthetic task domain, single model and validator, and absence of latency telemetry in the confirmatory artifacts. All code, inputs, raw outputs, and analysis artifacts are recorded in the execution manifest and hashes included in the evidence bundle.

sections.introduction: LLM-driven NetOps promises faster intent→configuration workflows but raises operational safety concerns: erroneous or unsafe configuration proposals can cause outages. Prior work has explored LLM-based configuration repair and verifier-augmented agents (e.g., formal verifiers, digital-twin assisted validation) to improve safety. Motivated by an operator SLO trade-off between verification latency and safety, we ask: Can a selective, low-latency verification tier (risk-scoring + fast validator) integrated into a generate–validate–repair pipeline materially reduce unsafe commits versus LLM-only while meeting a latency SLO? We preregistered a paired experiment (CAND-2026-001) comparing baseline (LLM-only) against guarded (selective verifier invoking a fast validator only for high-risk candidates). Contributions: (1) a fully preregistered confirmatory evaluation on 400 synthetic intents using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic netops validator; (2) complete archived execution and analysis artifacts (model calls, validator traces, paired contingency table); (3) an evidence-grounded assessment showing a very small absolute safety gain in this in-distribution synthetic corpus and a discussion of practical limits and next steps.
sections.related_work: Recent benchmarks and studies have examined LLM-driven configuration repair and agentic architectures that combine LLMs with verification tools and digital twins. Notable nearby efforts include functional benchmarks for configuration repair and agentic repair evaluations that pair LLMs with verification tooling. Work on verification-aware NetOps (formal verification, network digital twins, and verifier-assisted LLM agents) frames our reliability and design choices. We use these works for positioning and to motivate selective verification as an operationally realistic mitigation (see cited_record_ids).
sections.methodology: Design and preregistration: The confirmatory plan CAND-2026-001 (frozen before execution) defined (1) a paired binary design over 400 unique intents; (2) two conditions: baseline (LLM-only) and guarded (selective verifier invoked per a pretrained risk-classifier threshold); (3) primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; (4) inclusion of 10% adversarial/OOD deterministic variants; (5) prespecified missingness, retry, and analysis rules. Data and environment: We used a synthetic, shareable intent corpus generator (intent types: ACL edits, route additions/removals, interface edits) and a Dockerized digital-twin validator family supporting two vendor families. Model and pipeline: All generations used gpt-5-mini (declared model in execution manifest). The adapter/orchestration family was hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 served as the full-checker ground truth and scorer (scoring_rule: full_intent_constraint_validation). Execution contract: paired episodes = 400 tasks × 2 conditions = 800 episodes; planned maximum model calls = 800; actual model_calls_used = 401 (shared initial generation design; see execution manifest). Analysis plan: pre-specified paired McNemar-equivalent exact test via the paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor, exact binomial CIs for per-condition rates, paired bootstrap percentile CI for the estimand (10,000 resamples, seed frozen). All artifacts, traces, and hashes were preserved and are available in the execution manifest.
sections.results: Execution and primary confirmatory outcome: Execution completed per plan: 400 complete pairs, 0 failed episodes (execution manifest). Per-condition success (valid configuration per full-checker): baseline 399/400 (success rate 0.9975), guarded 400/400 (success rate 1.000). Contingency (paired) counts: n11=399, n10=1 (guarded=1, baseline=0), n01=0, n00=0. Primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) = 0.0025. Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% CI for difference: [0.0, 0.0075] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Interpretation: the guarded pipeline produced one additional success relative to baseline in this corpus; the absolute improvement (0.25 percentage points) is small and not distinguishable from zero at conventional levels given the observed discordance pattern. Secondary planned latency analyses and verification-budget Pareto curves were specified in the preregistration, but confirmatory secondary_results artifacts are absent from the provided analysis outputs; latency SLO (95th-percentile ≤ 2000 ms) therefore remains unresolved in the available confirmatory artifact set. Contamination/adversarial checks: the confirmatory corpus included the preregistered 10% adversarial variants; contamination_summary in analysis artifacts is empty (no flagged items reported). Representative per-episode scoring and validator traces are archived (example task JSONs and validator traces available in execution/scoring/).
sections.discussion: What the confirmatory outcome shows: In an in-distribution synthetic corpus where baseline LLM proposals are already highly accurate under a deterministic validator, a selective low-latency verifier produced one additional correct outcome out of 400 paired items. This indicates the mechanism can catch some rare failures but that absolute gains shrink when baseline success is near ceiling. Operational meaning: for operator contexts with already-high baseline correctness or where validator semantics and task distributions are similar to training data, the marginal safety benefit of an inexpensive selective verifier may be limited. Open questions and exploratory directions (from preregistration): (i) how gains scale with more adversarial/OOD distributions; (ii) the verification budget vs safety Pareto frontier (threshold sweeps); (iii) latency vs safety trade-offs with real telemetry. Practical guidance: selective verification is conceptually promising but must be calibrated and stress-tested on representative adversarial and production distributions; full latency telemetry and real-device semantics are required before deployment decisions.
sections.conclusion: We conducted a fully preregistered, artifact-backed paired confirmatory evaluation of a selective low-latency verification intervention applied to LLM-generated NetOps changes using gpt-5-mini. Results show a very small absolute safety improvement (one discordant pair in 400) with the guarded pipeline in this synthetic, in-distribution corpus; the improvement is not statistically distinguishable from zero in this test. Key limitations (single model, synthetic corpus, single deterministic validator, absent latency telemetry) constrain generalization. Future work should (1) evaluate across multiple models and real-device digital twins, (2) measure and optimize latency with full telemetry, and (3) explore adversarial robustness and threshold-calibration to map operational Pareto frontiers. All experiment code, inputs, outputs, and analysis artifacts are archived (see execution manifest hashes) to enable independent reproduction and further study.

limitations: Synthetic corpus: tasks were generated by a deterministic synthetic generator and may not reflect full production diversity.
Single model: experiments used only gpt-5-mini; results do not generalize across model families.
Single deterministic validator: safety labels derive from deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (digital-twin semantics); real-device behavior may differ.
Ceiling effect: baseline success rate was already very high (99.75%), limiting observable absolute gains.
Latency telemetry missing from confirmatory artifacts: preregistered H2 (latency SLO) could not be evaluated from provided analysis outputs.
